On Thu, Jan 6, 2022 at 10:03 AM Meral Karan <[contact omitted]> wrote:
Thanks Johnny. Definitely lots to mull over and possibly a great opportunity. I'm definitely interested in that threats
briefing - could we do it after our strategy discussion next week? That allows us all to get our ducks in a row more
broadly beforehand.
Anyone feel otherwise? Otherwise, I would just make sure Sabeen or folks at ITR are looped in too.
Thanks again,
M

On Thu, Jan 6, 2022 at 12:26 AM Johnny Walsh <[contact omitted]> wrote:
As I discussed with some of you beforehand, 1 met today with Facebook/Meta's Brian Rice (former Kerry staffer
and their overall lead for outreach to the Executive branch and Shaarik Zafar (former DOS Special Envoy to
Muslim Communities, now with the DC office's Public Policy team). Colin Thomas-Jensen passed them my way; it
was quite a positive meeting. Highlights:
- They led by saying they fully appreciate all the reasons people hate FB, but they/the company want to be leaders
in advancing democracy and countering digital authoritarianism. Thought S4D was a real success but wished it
had gone bigger and been more specific on the digital auth issue. (..and, of course, that there had been less
trashing of FB).
- Drawing on what Josh and Lorri sent, I offered three initial categories where | could imagine cooperating: FB
helping countries implement Summit commitments during the YOA, creating special access for USAID partners to
various FB perks (ad credits, audience data, etc etc), and expanding content moderation to places FB doesn't

adequately cover, including reference to B-Tech. We discussed each in quasi-detail, and Brian was extremely
positive on all three. He said we should work on details, but all are entirely within the realm of what FB could and
would do.
- As a next step, they proposed a sort of "threats briefing" where some of their team present the key digital
authoritarianism trends they're seeing, ostensibly to me but really to a group of us, and we can do likewise if we
see fit. Then if we all think the three buckets still make sense, we could do a dedicated meeting on each, with
whoever would be most interested.
Working with Meta is thorny, and we should have a group huddle to talk this through. At the same time, the degree
of willingness on their end to do specific things was striking, even if it comes from some amount of guilt/PR
desperation over the perception that their company broke the world. Would love to hear this group's reactions.
Also, Jason, sorry I didn't include you on an earlier note | sent teeing up this meeting. Are there other DRG folks
I'm forgetting who should be in on this?
Johnny Walsh
Deputy Assistant Administrator for Democracy, Human Rights, and Governance
U.S. Agency for International Development

Deputy Assistant Administrator for Democracy, Human Rights, and Governance
U.S. Agency for International Development
